brier_no_worse_than_baseline.rule: candidate forward Brier score on the frozen holdout must be <= baseline forward Brier score on the identical rows

forward_auc_exceeds_baseline.baseline_comparator: baseline_model.id = team_outcome_only_v0, i.e. the beta=0 candidate re-run over the same holdout rows
forward_auc_exceeds_baseline.paired_test_rule: Compare the two models as a PAIRED difference on identical rows, never as two independent AUCs. Report the paired bootstrap distribution of the AUC difference over series-clustered resamples, with its median and a two-sided 95% interval.
forward_auc_exceeds_baseline.rule: the PAIRED forward AUC difference (candidate minus team_outcome_only_v0) on the identical holdout rows must be strictly greater than zero
forward_auc_exceeds_baseline.statistical_power_disclosure: At n=35 the absolute AUC 95% interval is approximately +/-0.216 (SE ~0.110), so an unpaired comparison at this size cannot distinguish a real improvement from noise. The paired difference cancels between-game variance and is the only defensible comparison at this sample size. This limitation must be stated verbatim in any published promotion receipt issued at n<100.

identifiability_shrinkage_gate.rule: the published duplicate-group player count (see identifiability_diagnostic) computed under the candidate must be strictly lower than the team-outcome-only baseline's duplicate-group player count over the identical player/game population at the same n_maps thresholds (>=1 and >=20)

log_loss_no_worse_than_baseline.rule: candidate forward log loss on the frozen holdout must be <= baseline forward log loss on the identical rows

minimum_games_and_coverage_inventory_gat.coherence_note: The league sub-gate is restored to 3 leagues x 20 holdout games. It had been rescaled to 3 x 10 only because 3 x 20 = 60 could not fit inside a 35-game holdout; that constraint no longer binds at 100 (60 <= 100).
minimum_games_and_coverage_inventory_gat.note: mirrors public-draft-score-promotion-protocol-v39.json's inventory gates; open the sealed outcomes exactly once, only after every inventory gate passes
minimum_games_and_coverage_inventory_gat.owner_amendment: Owner restored minimum_holdout_games from 35 to 100 on 2026-08-17. Rationale: at n=35 the disclosed absolute AUC 95% interval is approximately +/-0.216, which could only ever yield evidence_strength "provisional_small_sample". Slower evidence is preferred over a provisional-only result. The 2026-08-17 lowering from 150 to 35 is superseded.

provisional_promotion_prohibited.reason: minimum_holdout_games (100) equals the former provisional threshold (100), so the provisional path is unreachable by construction. The dead rule was removed rather than left in the gate set.
provisional_promotion_prohibited.rule: No promotion under this protocol version may carry evidence_strength "provisional_small_sample".

series_cluster_bootstrap_median_auc_exce.rule: series-clustered bootstrap median AUC for the candidate must exceed the equivalent bootstrap median AUC for the baseline on the same resampled series

baseline_model.claim: descriptive; measures historical team results; does not identify individual causal contribution
baseline_model.definition: the current published build_player_ratings() pipeline, unmodified: every player on a side receives the identical (y - exp_b) or ((1-y)-(1-exp_b)) residual, scaled only by k_regional/k_meta, k_scale, and mov

attribution_input_source.note: grade_team is already: (1) role-and-league-or-tier normalized per metric via _historical_z before combining into _base, then (2) demeaned and standardized within the same game_id+side 5-player group. It is mean-zero across the 5 teammates in a map by construction, which is what makes it usable as a zero-sum split of a shared team residual. No raw CORE_INPUTS value is consumed directly by the attribution term.

candidate_attribution_parameterization.equation_blue: st.mu_regional += cfg.k_regional * k_scale * mov * (y - exp_b) * a_i(t)
candidate_attribution_parameterization.equation_red: st.mu_regional += cfg.k_regional * k_scale * mov * ((1 - y) - (1 - exp_b)) * a_i(t)
excluded_this_version: absolute_grading_channel (no team-outcome anchor; rejected, see zero_sum_vs_absolute_analysis)
additive_attribution_in_elo_points (rejected: decouples rating direction from win/loss sign)
any use of raw, non-role-normalized CORE_INPUTS values directly in the update

fallback_on_unavailable_grade.effect: reduces exactly to today's baseline update for that player-map; never fabricated
fallback_on_unavailable_grade.trigger: grade_status != 'available' for that player-map (per GRADE_CONTRACT: incomplete lineup, missing core inputs, or fewer than 10 prior self-comparable games)

role_specific_beta.selection_rule: fit only after the global-beta family is scored on the development folds; select the role-specific family only if its development-fold forward AUC exceeds the best global-beta family by a materially significant margin (owner-reviewed) under the same gates; otherwise the simplest identified parameterization (global beta) is frozen, per the closed-decision convention in docs/model-v2/research-register.md

invariants.attribution_nonnegative: floor >= 0.0 guarantees a_i >= 0 for all i
invariants.never_flips_residual_sign: because a_i >= 0, sign(update_i) == sign(y - exp_b); a poor individual statline in a win can shrink credit toward zero but never becomes a rating loss, and vice versa for a loss
invariants.team_mean_attribution_equals_one_before_: mean_i(1 + beta * grade_team_i) = 1 across the 5 teammates, because grade_team is mean-zero within team+game by construction
invariants.team_mean_attribution_near_one_after_sof: soft_clip is odd and smooth, so the post-clip team mean deviates from 1 only by higher-order curvature; must be monitored (see identifiability_diagnostic.zero_sum_drift_check), not assumed exact

cases.case: grade unavailable for one or both players on every shared map
cases.disclosure: the pair remains in the existing duplicate-group diagnostic, unresolved_reason='grade_unavailable'

cases.case: grade available but a_i is numerically identical for two teammates on every shared map (e.g., beta=0, or truly indistinguishable performance)
cases.disclosure: if resulting mu_total/mu_regional/mu_meta/sigma/n_maps remain equal within 1e-9 across the pair's full shared history, the pair is marked identifiability_status='tie_group' with a shared tie_group_id in the published snapshot; no synthetic epsilon, hash-based jitter, or arbitrary tie-break ordering may be introduced to force a visible difference

forbidden: silent omission of a known tie from the public snapshot
tie_handling.rule: never fabricate a difference the data does not support

zero_sum_vs_absolute_analysis.future_research_flag: an absolute (non-zero-sum) channel could in principle be explored later as a fully separate additive term structurally isolated from mu_regional/mu_meta (analogous to the existing momentum_scale/momentum_residual channel), but that is out of scope for this protocol and requires a new owner-approved research item before any design work begins.
reasoning: Zero-sum preserves the existing team-outcome calibration in aggregate: mean(a_i)~=1 means the total rating mass moved for a team-map is unchanged from today's baseline, only its allocation across the 5 teammates changes. This bounds regression risk to every downstream consumer of the aggregate team mu (draft-score ensemble strength inputs, p_player_elo, momentum).

Zero-sum cannot let a whole roster of stat-padders collectively out-earn what the team actually won on the scoreboard, and cannot let a whole roster collectively lose less than the team actually lost. It only re-ranks teammates against each other.

Absolute grading breaks the tie to wins: a high-stat performance in a loss could gain rating, or a low-stat performance in a win could lose rating, independent of the team result. This is the same failure mode that makes traditional raw KDA/damage 'grade' systems gameable by stat-padding in a loss, and it removes the natural budget constraint that keeps the update magnitude anchored to k_regional/k_meta*mov*(y-exp_b); an absolute channel needs its own separately-calibrated scale, which risks degrading forward AUC/Brier/log-loss below baseline and failing the acceptance gates outright.

Zero-sum's known cost: if two teammates truly have indistinguishable individual performance in every shared map, zero-sum split still cannot separate them (a_i equal for both). This is accepted and must be disclosed via the tie-group marker (see tie_handling), never papered over.

established_diagnosis.conclusion: collinear teammates are non-identifiable under a team-outcome-only model; this is expected, not a bug
only_per_player_terms: k_scale = st.sigma / cfg.sigma0 (deterministic decay, not skill-derived)
established_diagnosis.root_cause_expression_red: st.mu_regional += cfg.k_regional * k_scale * mov * ((1 - y) - (1 - exp_b))

verified_scale.example_clean_player_symdiff: Canyon 257 games, symdiff >= 2 vs nearest duplicate candidate
verified_scale.present_since: every locally available pack back to 2026-07-25; the update expression is unchanged since the repository's initial commit

fail_closed_rule.no_fabrication_rule: a failed or inconclusive gate may never be papered over with a hand-tuned constant, a synthetic tie-break, or a partial rollout that bypasses the gate set above
fail_closed_rule.statement: if any gate in acceptance_gates fails, the currently published team-outcome-only player rating model (lol_kills/ratings/player_elo.py as of this protocol's freeze) remains the production model. No partial promotion, no silent parameter change, and no re-fit-and-retry against the same sealed holdout is permitted. A failed attempt requires a new protocol version and a new frozen prospective holdout before any further candidate may be evaluated.

frozen_prospective_holdout.definition: every accepted, complete-lineup map with date >= start_inclusive, accumulated going forward from the freeze date of this protocol; sealed in the same append-only, receipt-based manner as the Draft Score holdout batches (never replace a sealed batch; use a new path per batch)
frozen_prospective_holdout.reseal_on_candidate_change: any change to beta, z_clip, floor, the role-specific decision, or the attribution equation itself invalidates every previously sealed batch for promotion purposes and starts a new holdout, exactly as changing a bound file starts a new holdout under protocol v39
frozen_prospective_holdout.sealing_procedure: prepare_selective_..._holdout-style: strip outcome/result fields from the feature and player rows before any candidate inference, run the frozen selected candidate (from training_windows.selection_rule) to produce forward player-Elo/win-probability forecasts, seal the sealed batch and its receipt with a SHA-256, and only then may a minimal outcomes file be joined

identifiability_diagnostic.cadence: computed and published every refresh/release, both for the currently published model and, during development, for each evaluated candidate
identifiability_diagnostic.computation: group all published players by the byte-identical tuple (mu_total, mu_regional, mu_meta, sigma, n_maps) rounded to the same precision the public snapshot already uses; a group of size >= 2 is a duplicate/tie group
identifiability_diagnostic.publication_requirement: this diagnostic must be written to a content-addressed JSON artifact under data/lol/v2/evaluation/ every release and referenced from a public-facing disclosure surface; it may not be computed and discarded, and it may not be an internal-only log line

published_fields.duplicate_group_size_histogram: object, group size -> count of groups
published_fields.model_id: team_outcome_only_v0 or the promoted candidate id
published_fields.tie_group_disclosures: list of {tie_group_id, players, reason} per tie_handling.cases above

zero_sum_drift_check.rule: for a sample of team-maps per release, report the mean and max absolute deviation of mean_i(a_i) from 1.0 across each 5-player team-map; this is a monitoring diagnostic, not a gate, but a persistent large drift blocks promotion pending owner review

independent_reviewer.independence_basis: The reviewer is a separate agent and toolchain from the automation that executes the candidate fit. The fitting run is executed by the Claude Code session; the review is executed by Codex. Neither may perform the other role for a given receipt.
independent_reviewer.independence_condition: The reviewer must not author, tune, or execute the fitting run, and must not select parameter values.
independent_reviewer.owner_role: The owner (River) is NOT the reviewer under this version and may therefore direct parameter and grid decisions without voiding the assignment.
independent_reviewer.supersedes_assignment: River (owner) as reviewer, assigned under protocol v2
independent_reviewer.void_condition: If the Codex reviewer is used to perform or tune the fitting run, this assignment is void and a different reviewer must be named before a receipt is issued.

leakage_constraint.enforcement: identical in spirit to the sealed-holdout mechanism in data/lol/v2/evaluation/public-draft-score-promotion-protocol-v39.json: development-fold selection happens first and is fully separate from the single frozen prospective holdout, which is sealed by game_uid/date range before any outcome in it is read for evaluation purposes
forbidden: scoring a candidate by whether grade_team_i correlates with game t's own outcome (trivially true by construction and uninformative)
any metric that is computed from, or averaged over, the outcome-labeled window used to evaluate forward prediction
refitting beta/z_clip/floor after opening the frozen prospective holdout defined below
leakage_constraint.statement: in-game metrics (CORE_INPUTS, and any grade derived from them) are contemporaneous with the outcome of game t. They may inform the per-player attribution applied to the rating UPDATE that follows game t (redistributing an outcome-anchored residual that was already computed from pre-game mu's), but the ATTRIBUTION PARAMETERIZATION (beta, z_clip, floor, and any role-specific variant) may only be selected and evaluated by whether the RESULTING RATINGS predict games strictly after the games used to fit them.

metric_set.ece_10: ten-bin expected calibration error, same holdout, same prediction stream
metric_set.forward_auc: AUC of the sequential win-probability output (p_player_elo or its candidate-updated equivalent) against y_blue_win, computed strictly out-of-sample on the frozen holdout using only ratings state as of just before each holdout game
metric_set.series_cluster_bootstrap: series-clustered bootstrap median AUC, mirroring public-draft-score-promotion-protocol-v39.json's series_cluster_bootstrap_median_auc_minimum, to avoid multi-map-series pseudo-replication inflating apparent significance

out_of_scope_this_protocol: fitting, training, or evaluating any candidate (design and protocol only)
any change to lol_kills/ratings/player_elo.py or any other production rating code
any refresh, publish, or promotion action
the absolute (non-zero-sum) attribution channel described in zero_sum_vs_absolute_analysis.future_research_flag
the separate v2 dynamic Player Rating track under lol_kills/v2/ratings/player/

reaffirmed: open sealed outcomes exactly once after inventory gates pass

confirm the free-parameter ranges and candidate grids in candidate_attribution_parameterization.free_parameters

owner_decision.authorized_direction: individual in-game metrics should affect ratings (game grade, CS/min, damage/min, role-weighted KDA, gold share %, damage share %)
owner_decision.weighting_method: mathematically determined by fitting to what best predicts winning, the same way the Draft Score composite was selected; no hand-picked constants

problem_statement: The public player Dual-Elo baseline (lol_kills/ratings/player_elo.py) applies one team-outcome residual to every player on a side with only a fixed role weight and a per-player sigma-decay scale as differentiators. Teammates who share an identical game set therefore receive byte-identical mu_total/mu_regional/mu_meta/sigma/n_maps. This is a proven non-identifiability of the current update, not a code defect. This protocol binds a candidate fix, its forward-chaining evaluation, and its promotion gates. It does not fit, train, or evaluate anything.

binds: the candidate attribution implementation file SHA-256
the sealed holdout batch receipt SHA-256(es), in chronological order
the minimal outcomes file SHA-256 used to open the seal
the baseline (beta=0) re-run receipt SHA-256 on the identical holdout rows
every acceptance_gates value actually observed, pass/fail per gate
the identifiability_diagnostic artifact SHA-256, before and after
a false betting/odds/EV/stake flag, matching every other promotion receipt in this repository
promotion_receipt_shape.unlock_condition: only a receipt of exactly this schema_version, with every acceptance_gates entry recorded as pass, may flip the production player-rating pipeline from team_outcome_only_v0 to the promoted candidate; a hash-shaped placeholder fails closed

related_but_distinct_track.note: lol_kills/v2/ratings/player/ implements a separate, development-only dynamic Player Rating (issue #45 acceptance record) that also targets this non-identifiability via a joint rank-one Gaussian attribution over player-specific pre-event information. That track is materially larger in scope, remains gated behind its own multi-stage acceptance protocol (protocol-lock-v1/v2, R-01 through R-21 in docs/model-v2/research-register.md), and is not reused or superseded by this protocol. This protocol is a narrower, surgical amendment to the existing published descriptive baseline only.

normalization_chain: each of the 8 METRICS in player_map_grades.py is z-scored per (league, role), falling back to (competition_tier, role), then (role) alone, against a strictly prior-calendar-day historical baseline (_historical_z), so a support's wards/min is compared only to other supports' history, never to a mid laner's
the 8 role-normalized z-scores are averaged into _base per player-map

_team demeans _base within the same game_id+side 5-player group (which mixes roles) and divides by the in-map team standard deviation, which is legitimate only because _base was already role-normalized upstream
role_normalization_contract.requirement: the attribution term must consume only the already role-normalized grade_team component; it must never consume raw CORE_INPUTS (kills, dpm, damageshare, cspm, wpm, wcpm, ...) directly
role_normalization_contract.role_neutrality_gate: per release, the mean attribution multiplier a_i must be reported by role (top/jng/mid/bot/sup) over the full development window; the protocol requires this to be published as a diagnostic, and a persistent, materially large mean deviation by role (owner-reviewed, no automatic numeric threshold prescribed here) blocks promotion pending root-cause review of the underlying metric normalization

training_windows.fold_rule: for fold k, run the sequential player-Elo replay exactly as today through train_end_exclusive with candidate (beta, z_clip, floor) applied from the start of the sequence, then score forward, unseen games in [eval_start, eval_end_exclusive) only; a game's own grade_team values may feed the update applied after that game finishes, but its label may never be used to pick beta/z_clip/floor

selection_rule.beta_0_baseline_check: the beta=0 candidate must reproduce the current published baseline's forward metrics on every development fold within floating-point tolerance; a mismatch invalidates the whole candidate grid and blocks selection
selection_rule.candidate_family_precedence: global beta first; role-specific beta only per the role_specific_beta.selection_rule above
selection_rule.metric: mean forward AUC across the 5 development folds (equal weight)
selection_rule.tie_breaker: lower mean forward Brier score across the 5 development folds
